title: Sensitive tax IDs stored as plaintext: the encrypted cast was never added
business_context: VaultDocs stores each customer's government tax ID (sensitive PII) alongside their profile. Compliance mandates encryption at rest: the column must never contain the plaintext value — anyone with database access (a dump, a replica, a backup) must not be able to read tax IDs directly. The application transparently encrypts on write and decrypts on read.
user_request: A security review found the customers.tax_id column contains the tax IDs in PLAINTEXT in the database. The application works perfectly — support reads and writes tax IDs through the app without issues — which is exactly why nobody noticed. Fix the storage so tax IDs are encrypted at rest while everything keeps working through the app exactly as before. The compliance audit re-checks the raw column.

intentional_defect.summary: The Customer model never declares an 'encrypted' cast for tax_id: Eloquent stores the plaintext value directly into the column.
intentional_defect.root_cause: Without the 'encrypted' cast, Eloquent passes the attribute to the database as-is. The application-level round-trip works identically with or without the cast, which is why no test or user ever noticed.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: The model, controller and endpoints are all correct: values round-trip, nothing errors, and the visible tests exercise the round-trip — the plaintext is only visible in the raw column.

non_obvious_invariant: The raw column value must be ciphertext (decryptable with the app key back to the plaintext tax ID), while the application-level round-trip stays transparent.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must recognize that the round-trip working says nothing about encryption at rest — the raw column must be inspected — and add Laravel's 'encrypted' cast to the model.
safe_fix_constraints: The application-level behavior stays identical: support reads and writes tax IDs through the app exactly as before.
The raw column must contain ciphertext decryptable with the app key (not a homemade obfuscation such as base64).
failure_explanation: Any database dump, replica, backup or compromised credential exposes every customer's tax ID in plaintext — a direct PII compliance violation. The column reads as a normal string column, so the exposure is invisible until an audit inspects the raw data.
